chapter: Decca, Cow Cow Blues and royalties
title: Touring costs in Germany, living simply, and his Boogie-Woogie records
summary: He explains how little profit a German trip leaves, his frugal habits, and that he has made over a hundred Boogie-Woogie records.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: When I went to Germany right now, and it cost me, believe me...see, it cost me four hundred and forty dollars and then five hundred and eighty,-- all right?--to make $2500. So my profit is fifteen hundred dollars which is not fair to me because, you know, that's not really...you know...I've got to travel, you know what I mean, a great distance, and then I've gotta appear, I've gotta be there, you know what I mean, then you've got to buy your food and, you know, but I'm very conservative about my eating because, you know, I don't have to have like

caviar and I think I'll try the wine of the region. I never do these things, see, because I don't drink anyway. So just give me very simple food and a nice, clean room with a shower and bath because I'm finishing up my book, you know what I mean, and then I can...I'm happy. But I don't know... I really don't know what to say as far as what... if I've made a contribution musically. That, history will have to determine, and usually they don't decide whether you've done anything until after you're dead and gone. Because, believe me...you know, you and I've been friends over the years, and I never had the slightest idea that I would be as close to you in the last two months as I've been, which is amazing, see. And then the fact that the contribution may be now or it may be in the future, or that [it] may start...you know, I've made over a hundred Boogie-Woogie records. I don't have 'em, you know. But I've made Boogie-Woogie in every country. I've made from the "Denmark Boogie" to the "Muenchen Boogie". The "Barbarian Blues"...you know. And I just...I do it as a lark, because when I do it it's funny on stage, but the people like the music. And the Boogie-Woogie... it's the same thing isn't it. You know, Boogie-Woogie's just a movement, Boogie-Woogie is that same movement that Blind Lemon Jefferson played on the guitar.

I heard it. So nobody can tell me any different. See, I heard it. I heard it in 1916, '17, '18 and on until, you know, and I could still hear "The Penitentiary Blues" and those things that he did. But some people will try to take credit for it... Jay and Ray in Switzerland and all that shit, but I heard it. And until somebody proves different, that's how it is.

But I have never been so inspired as a pianist as I have been by Art Tatum. I've been influenced by him. And I don't play anything like him. The only thing Art Tatum taught me was to get a tone out of the piano.
